ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Nocturnal pauses

A 61-year-old is referred after a sleep monitor recorded sinus slowing and brief pauses overnight. He has loud snoring, witnessed apneas and daytime somnolence but no daytime syncope. Which evaluation should be prioritized before assuming that he needs a permanent pacemaker?

  1. Assessment for obstructive sleep apnea
  2. Electrophysiologic ablation of the sinus node
  3. Coronary angiography solely for the pauses
  4. Routine permanent pacing based only on the nocturnal rate
  5. Exercise restriction without further assessment
Answer and explanation

Assessment for obstructive sleep apnea

Sleep-disordered breathing can produce nocturnal bradyarrhythmia and should be evaluated.

Option explanations

Assessment for obstructive sleep apnea: Sleep-disordered breathing can produce nocturnal bradyarrhythmia and should be evaluated.

Electrophysiologic ablation of the sinus node: Sinus-node ablation would worsen slowing.

Coronary angiography solely for the pauses: No ischemic features are provided to justify angiography on this basis alone.

Routine permanent pacing based only on the nocturnal rate: Nocturnal bradycardia alone is not a permanent pacing indication.

Exercise restriction without further assessment: Avoidance of activity does not address the likely sleep-related mechanism.
